adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65 — `params.require(:usernames)` runs before the automatic-group guard, so a missing param yields 400 instead of the intended 422 (P2, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` before `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`. In Rails, `params.require` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when absent, which results in a 400 response before the automatic-group guard can run. So for an automatic group request missing `usernames`, the controller would return 400 instead of the intended 422 `can_not_modify_automatic` response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8 — public members page gained no pagination controls, so groups >50 members are silently truncated with no way to reach the rest (P1, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit` of 50 for *all* groups (not just automatic ones), and returns a paginated JSON payload (`members` + `meta`). On the public members page, `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now just sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()` with no way to change `offset`. The public template `group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}`, but there are no pagination controls/actions added on the public members page (unlike the admin group UI which gained next/previous). Therefore groups with >50 members will only show the first page and the rest are unreachable from the UI, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:11 — off-by-one totalPages (should be Math.ceil): 50 members/limit 50 reports 2 pages and the last renders empty (P2, conf 95)
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` silently drops unknown usernames and still returns success_json; no error surfaced, no spec (P2, conf 95)

adjudication.rationale: The code at `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` does indeed ignore unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`) and will still return `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if no users were added. However, this is not a clear defect introduced by the diff: the prior implementation (`update_patch`) had the same “silent success when adding non-existent users” behavior, and the removed specs even explicitly asserted this was acceptable. The lack of an error or spec here is therefore not a verifiable problem on its own, but an intentional/consistent behavior choice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65 — `usernames.split(",")` without strip, so `"a, b"` fails to resolve `" b"`; empty input raises ParameterMissing 400 instead of a 422/no-op (P2, conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end`. There is no `strip`/whitespace normalization on each split token, so an input like `"a, b"` will produce a token `" b"` that will not match a username `"b"`, causing that member not to be added. Also, because it uses `params.require(:usernames)`, a request that omits the `usernames` parameter will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (typically a 400) rather than being handled as a 422 or a no-op in this action. Both behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` for a non-member/nonexistent id is untested and may raise RecordNotFound instead of succeeding silently (P2, conf 60)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an integer. In Rails, `has_many`/HABTM association `delete` with an id typically issues a DELETE against the join/association records and does not raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` when the id is not currently associated (or even when no join row exists); it just results in 0 rows affected. The diff also doesn’t show any code path that would convert this into a `find`/`destroy!` call that could raise. The finding is therefore speculative (and “untested” isn’t itself a verifiable defect in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` unvalidated: limit=0/negative errors, limit=100000 dumps a whole group; no spec for the new meta envelope at all (P1, conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes both straight into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounds checking. This is verifiably risky/correctness-impacting: a client can request an extremely large `limit` (or potentially a negative value) causing very large result sets or DB errors (e.g., negative offset), which is a real performance/robustness problem introduced by the change. The “no spec for the new meta envelope” part is more about test coverage than a direct defect, but the unvalidated pagination params issue is real in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — empty-name path returns undefined instead of `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`, so `.then` chains in addMembers/removeMember throw (P2, conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `findMembers` was changed to `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`, so it can return `undefined` instead of a promise. However, the proposed impact is not verifiable from the diff: `addMembers`/`removeMember` do not chain `.then` off `findMembers` (they call `self.findMembers();` inside an ajax `.then` without using its return value), and the routes/controllers updated in this diff call `model.findMembers()` without chaining as well. So while the return-type change exists, the specific claim that it makes `.then` chains in `addMembers/removeMember` throw is a misreading and not demonstrated by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — after add/remove, findMembers refetches the stale offset; deleting the last member of the final page leaves currentPage > totalPages (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. After `removeMember` / `addMembers`, the model calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset` (group.js `removeMember` and `addMembers`). In `findMembers`, the requested offset is clamped using the *current* `user_count` (`var ... offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`), which can be stale immediately after a deletion. The server endpoint (`GroupsController#members`) does not clamp `offset` to the new total; it echoes back `meta.offset = offset` and can return an empty `members` array when `offset` is now beyond the end. The client then sets `user_count` to the new smaller total but keeps `offset` at the too-large value, making `currentPage = floor(offset/limit)+1` potentially greater than `totalPages` (e.g., being on offset=50, limit=50, deleting down to total=49 yields currentPage=2 while totalPages=1). This is a concrete correctness issue introduced/left by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:120 — no tests for re-adding an existing member, index search/ignore_automatic params, the create error branch, or non-admin rejection of the new member routes (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The finding is about missing test coverage (re-adding existing member, index params, create failure branch, non-admin access). While it’s true the diff adds new endpoints/behaviors and the updated spec does not include those cases, lack of tests is not itself a verifiable functional/security defect introduced by the diff—especially since Admin::GroupsController inherits from Admin::AdminController, which already enforces admin-only access irrespective of explicit tests. Therefore this is a coverage suggestion rather than a concrete bug/security issue evidenced in the diff.

However, this is paired with corresponding client-side changes: the Group model’s asJSON() now emits a flat payload without usernames, the admin controller now calls group.create()/group.save() (not *WithUsernames), and membership is moved to new dedicated endpoints (add_members/remove_member) that the JS uses. So within the diff, this is a coordinated API change rather than a verifiable defect/regression in the updated code paths; claims that it’s “not required”/a “breaking CRUD change” are subjective and depend on external API consumers not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:49 — `get "users"` admin route removed alongside the new member routes; unrelated deletion with no covering spec (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `get "users"` under the admin `groups` resource being replaced by `delete "members"` / `put "members"`, which appears to be an intentional API change to support the new add/remove member endpoints. There is no evidence in the provided diff that anything still references the removed `users` route (no remaining calls to `/admin/groups/.../users`), so claiming it’s an “unrelated deletion” or a defect is speculative. Lack of a spec specifically asserting that old route exists is not, by itself, a verifiable correctness problem introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:52 — `// TODO: should clear the input`: after adding, usernames stay in the selector and a second click re-submits them (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` but never clears/resets the controller’s `usernames` property afterward. Since the template’s `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` is two-way bound to that property, the entered usernames will remain in the selector UI after the add completes, and clicking the Add button again will re-submit the same usernames. The inline `// TODO: should clear the input` comment confirms this missing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — pagination now applies to all groups but only the admin template got next/prev controls; public group pages silently truncate at 50 (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes behavior from only paginating automatic groups (and otherwise returning the full ordered list) to *always* applying `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit` of 50:

```rb
limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i
...
members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)
```

On the public members page, the route now calls `model.findMembers()` (which uses the default `limit: 50, offset: 0`) and the template renders `{{#each m in members}}` with no next/prev controls added in the public `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`. Only the *admin* group template gains pagination controls.

Result: public group members pages will show only the first 50 users by default, with no UI to reach subsequent pages. That’s a concrete, verifiable regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:27 — bare array response replaced by `{members:, meta:}`; public endpoint shape break with no spec coverage (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the response changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns the serialized members collection directly) to an explicit wrapper object `{ members: ..., meta: ... }`. That is an observable API/endpoint contract change for `/groups/:group_id/members` (now `/members.json` is used by the updated client), and the diff includes no controller spec coverage for this public endpoint to confirm compatibility or intended break. This is directly verifiable from the diff and can break existing consumers expecting an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb — deleted incremental-membership tests have no replacement under add_members/remove_member though the silent-skip semantics remain (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior incremental-membership specs (PATCH add/delete, non-existent user add, removing non-members) and introduces new endpoints/spec contexts for add_members/remove_member, but it does not add equivalent tests for the old “silent skip” behaviors. However, this is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the code itself. The finding points to missing tests, not a functional problem in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb — `xhr :put, :remove_member` hardcodes group 1 as automatic and uses PUT while the route is DELETE, so the DELETE wiring is untested (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the remove_member endpoint is wired as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, and the client-side model correctly calls it with `type: "DELETE"`. However, in spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb the new remove_member spec uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which does not match the routed verb. As a result, the spec would not verify the DELETE route wiring and is inconsistent with the intended API usage shown elsewhere in the diff. The spec also assumes `group_id: 1` refers to an automatic group (as done in other new specs), which is a hardcoded assumption.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:78 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an Integer to a has_many collection proxy; removal may raise or silently no-op (P0, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` is an Integer and the code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. For a typical Rails `has_many :users` / `has_many :through` association, `collection.delete` expects AR model instances (or arrays of instances) and will raise `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` when given a plain Integer, rather than removing the user from the association. The earlier code paths in this diff used `group.remove(user)` (i.e., a User object), which avoids this. So this is a concrete correctness bug introduced here (potential runtime exception / failure to remove).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — no upper cap on `limit` on a public endpoint recreates unbounded materialization; a negative limit yields `LIMIT -1` StatementInvalid (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or validation. That makes the public `members` endpoint vulnerable to requesting arbitrarily large pages (e.g., `?limit=1000000`) and potentially unbounded result sets (negative limits may be treated as “no limit” by some adapters/DBs). The specific claim that a negative limit will *definitely* raise `StatementInvalid` is not provable from the diff (behavior varies), but the core issue—no cap/validation on `limit` allowing excessive materialization—is real and verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:63 — `usernames.split(",").each { User.find_by_username(username) }` is an N+1 over an uncapped client-supplied list; should be one `User.where(username_lower: names)` (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end`. This issues one query per supplied username (classic N+1 over the input list) and there is no cap/limit on how many comma-separated usernames the client can send, so a large list can cause many DB lookups in a single request. This is directly verifiable in the diff and could be addressed by batching (e.g., `User.where(username_lower: ...)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:12 — `Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1` off-by-one leaves Next enabled onto a phantom empty page on every exact page-size multiple (P1, conf 100)
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe the same pagination off-by-one behavior where, when the total user_count is an exact multiple of the page size (limit), the UI allows navigating to a 'next' page that has no results (offset equals total), creating a phantom empty last page and confusing UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20 — sentinel meaning change: `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` → `undefined`, so any `.then` on the unnamed-group path throws (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#findMembers` the early-exit changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);` to `return;` when `name` is empty. That is a real behavioral/API change: the method no longer consistently returns a promise, and any existing caller that does `group.findMembers().then(...)` (as the removed routes previously did) would now hit `undefined.then` when `name` is blank. Even though the updated call sites in this diff no longer chain `.then`, the regression is present in the method itself and is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:29 and config/routes.rb:49 — response reshaped to `{members:, meta:}` and `get "users"` removed: unversioned API-contract break for existing clients/plugins (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the `GroupsController#members` response from a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to a new JSON object shape: `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. Any existing client code (including plugins/theme JS) expecting the old array payload from `/groups/:group_id/members(.json)` will break. Separately, `config/routes.rb` removes the previous `get "users"` route under `admin/groups` and replaces it with `put/delete "members"`, which is also an API/route contract change for any callers of the old endpoint. Both are directly verifiable in the diff and represent backward-incompatible changes without versioning/compat shims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — `create` never reads `alias_level` though the client's asJSON sends it; the admin's selection is silently discarded (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` the client includes `alias_level` (and `save`/`create` send that payload). However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` and never assigns `group.alias_level` from params. As a result, when creating a new group, any alias level chosen in the admin UI is ignored and the group will be created with the model/default alias_level instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:63 — check-then-insert per username with no unique index or transaction; double submit creates duplicate group_users, and `group.save` after `group.add` makes render_json_error unreachable (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` iterates `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user, then `group.save` to decide success vs `render_json_error`. The proposed finding hinges on two claims that are not verifiable from the diff: (1) that there is "no unique index or transaction" so double-submit creates duplicate `group_users` rows—schema/indices and `Group#add` behavior are not shown here, and Discourse commonly enforces uniqueness at the DB level; and (2) that `render_json_error` is unreachable because `group.save` after `group.add` cannot fail—this depends on model validations/callbacks not present in the diff. The code shown does not contain a check-then-insert pattern either; it simply attempts to add each user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — `group.users.count` re-counts per page while a `user_count` column exists and is never updated by add/remove; two sources of truth drift and the header count goes stale (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `total = group.users.count` is intentionally computing the total number of members (not “per page”), and that value is returned as `meta.total`. On the client side, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` explicitly sets `user_count: result.meta.total`, so the header count is refreshed from the server and will not go stale due to the `user_count` column. The claim that a `user_count` column exists “and is never updated by add/remove” is not verifiable from this diff (membership changes call `group.add(user)` / `group.users.delete`, whose counter behavior is outside the shown changes). At most, this could be a performance consideration, not a demonstrated correctness defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — offset clamped inclusive to user_count, so offset == total is legal and next() can land on a non-multiple offset making currentPage non-integer (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:37 — add/remove unconditionally refetch with the stale offset; removing the last member of the final page strands the user on an empty page (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, both addMembers() and removeMember() call self.findMembers() without adjusting the pagination offset. findMembers() computes the request offset using the *current* (pre-refetch) user_count: `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`. After removing a member on the last page, the true total can drop below the current offset (e.g., total 51, limit 50, offset 50 -> remove 1 => total 50 but offset still 50). Because the clamp uses stale user_count (51), it will still request offset 50, and the server will return an empty page. The code does not correct offset based on the new `result.meta.total`, so the UI can strand the user on an empty final page after removal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:12 — findMembers moved from afterModel to setupController with the promise discarded: loading state, error handling and test determinism lost (P2, conf 100)
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:30 — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is stringly-typed: a JSON boolean `true` sets visible to false (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the JS client sends `visible` via `Discourse.ajax(..., data: this.asJSON())`, which (as typical for jQuery-style form encoding) serializes booleans to the strings "true"/"false". The updated controller code (`params[:visible] == "true"`) matches that behavior, and the updated controller spec explicitly passes `visible: "true"`, reinforcing that the expected type is a string. While it’s true that a *JSON* boolean `true` would not equal the string "true", nothing in this diff shows requests being sent as JSON booleans, so the finding is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:30 — update no longer guards alias_level/visible for automatic groups while destroy/add_members/remove_member all do; inconsistent invariant (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, automatic groups still can have `alias_level` and `visible` changed, but this is not a new behavior introduced by the diff: the old `update_put` also set `group.alias_level` and `group.visible` before checking `group.automatic` and only skipped rename/membership changes for automatic groups. The diff mainly refactors update/create payload shape and moves membership changes into separate endpoints guarded by `group.automatic`. So the claim that `update` “no longer guards” these fields for automatic groups is a misreading/regression claim not supported by the prior code, and the “inconsistent invariant” is not verifiably a defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb — the whole `update_patch` incremental add/delete membership API is deleted rather than fixed; consumers of PATCH with `changes:{add,delete}` lose membership handling (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete `update_patch` and removes PATCH-based incremental membership changes from `Admin::GroupsController#update`. However, the same diff adds dedicated membership endpoints (`add_members` via PUT and `remove_member` via DELETE) and updates the JS model/controller to use `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` instead. There is no remaining in-repo consumer shown that still calls PATCH with `changes:{add,delete}`; the removed specs for PATCH also indicate this behavior was intentionally retired. Any breakage for external/unknown consumers is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — public members endpoint gains an envelope and a default 50-row truncation: unversioned contract break shipped under a "fix membership handling" task (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to an object envelope `{ members: ..., meta: ... }`. It also changes pagination behavior: previously only automatic groups applied `limit`/`offset` (default limit 200) while non-automatic returned the full ordered member list; now all groups apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, truncating to 50 by default. Even though the Ember client in this diff updates `Discourse.Group#findMembers` to expect the new envelope and pass limit/offset, any other consumers of this public endpoint would see a contract break and silent truncation. This is a verifiable behavioral/API change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — public members list renders only the first 50 with no pagination UI; net behavior loss rather than a fix (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes the public group members route to call `model.findMembers()` which now requests `/groups/<name>/members.json` with `limit` defaulting to 50 (see `Discourse.Group` `limit: 50` and `GroupsController#members` default `(params[:limit] || 50)`). `findMembers` sets `members` on the group model, and `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, so it will render only that limited page. There is no pagination UI or actions added to the public `group/members` template/route/controller in this diff (pagination controls were only added to the admin group template/controller). This is a verifiable behavior regression: only the first 50 members will display with no way to navigate further.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js — create no longer posts `usernames` and the member UI is gated behind `{{#if id}}`; the one-step create-with-members workflow is removed without stated acceptance (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change behavior: `Discourse.Group#create` now POSTs only `{name, alias_level, visible}` (no `usernames`), and `group.hbs` wraps the members/add-members UI in `{{#if id}}`, so you can’t add members until after the group is created. However, this is a deliberate workflow change (members are now managed via separate `add_members/remove_member` endpoints after creation) and is not inherently a bug/correctness defect shown by the diff. The finding’s “without stated acceptance” portion is speculative and not verifiable from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:49 — `get "users"` deleted with no replacement or spec, unrelated to the membership fix (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the removed `get "users"` under the admin `groups` resource is replaced by new member-management routes: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`. This is directly related to the membership changes in the diff (new `add_members`/`remove_member` controller actions and corresponding JS model methods calling `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`). Specs were also added/updated for these new endpoints (`.add_members`, `.remove_member` contexts). So the claim that it was deleted “with no replacement” and “unrelated” is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs and admin_base.scss:164 — an admin form/style redesign (including the unrelated badges area) is carried along with the membership fix (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a broader UI/CSS refactor: `group.hbs` is restructured into a `<form class="form-horizontal">`, button classes change, and `admin_base.scss` moves `.form-horizontal` styling from `section.details` to a new `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` block and adds additional `.groups`-specific rules. However, this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the change—it's a scope/cleanup concern (unrelated styling changes bundled with functional membership/pagination work), which is subjective and not inherently incorrect based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb — the documented tolerant-membership semantics tests are deleted rather than re-asserted; automatic-group rejection silently changed 403 → 422 (P2, conf 75)
app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound lets any user dump an entire group roster in one request (enumeration + DoS) (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no maximum/clamping. This allows a client who can access the endpoint to request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing the server to query and serialize a very large set of users in a single request (potentially heavy DB load and large response). The diff itself contains no other safeguard (e.g., max limit) in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — negative offset/limit reach Postgres unclamped (validation exists only client-side in group.js), producing 500s (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no server-side clamp/validation to prevent negative values. A request with `offset=-1` can propagate to SQL `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (OFFSET must not be negative), producing a 500. Client-side clamping in `group.js` does not protect against crafted requests, so the issue is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — update applies visible/alias_level without the `group.automatic` guard used by destroy/add_members/remove_member, and omitting `visible` silently hides the group (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff intentionally allows updating `visible` and `alias_level` even for automatic groups (it only guards renaming via `!group.automatic`). This matches the prior behavior: the old `update_put` also always applied `group.alias_level` and `group.visible` regardless of `group.automatic`, and the updated spec explicitly expects `visible` to change on an automatic group. The claim about a missing `group.automatic` guard is therefore a misread.

The note that omitting `visible` would set it to false (`params[:visible] == "true"`) is technically true, but it was also true before (old code did `payload[:visible] == "true"`), and PUT semantics commonly expect full payloads. So this is not a new, clearly verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65 — `usernames.split(",")` on an array-form param raises NoMethodError → 500 rather than 400 (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, a request can supply `usernames` as an array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), in which case `params[:usernames]` is an `Array` and `split` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. The diff does not add any type check/coercion to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:31 — only the negative rename case is tested; an implementation that never assigns `name` still passes (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an update implementation that *does* assign `group.name = params[:name]` when the group is not automatic, and adds a spec that only asserts the *negative* case (automatic groups ignore name changes). While it’s true there is no spec covering the positive rename path for non-automatic groups, that is a test-coverage critique rather than a concrete defect introduced by the diff. The finding claims a P1 implementation risk, but the actual code shown already assigns `name` appropriately, so there is no verifiable bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:30 — `alias_level` assignment in the rewritten update has zero coverage (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `Admin::GroupsController#update` to assign `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`. In the shown spec changes, the new `.update` coverage only asserts that an automatic group ignores `name` changes and does update `visible`; there is no assertion exercising `alias_level`. However, this is a test-coverage/process concern rather than a concrete functional defect, and the provided diff is truncated near the end of the spec (so additional tests could exist beyond what’s shown). As stated with "conf 100", it’s not a fully verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — create's `visible` default branch is untested; every group created without explicit visible=true is invisible and no test catches it (P2, conf 100)
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:26 — the `render_json_error group` failure path of create is untested (P3, conf 100)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:69 — the silent-skip branch for unknown usernames lost its covering spec ("succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" deleted, not replaced) (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In the old spec suite under the `.update` incremental PATCH tests, there was an explicit example `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"`, exercising the behavior that unknown usernames are ignored without error. In the new implementation, this behavior still exists in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (it does `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`, so unknown usernames are silently skipped), but the covering spec was removed and no equivalent test was added under the new `.add_members` context (only tests for automatic-group rejection and adding valid users exist). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:88 — "succeeds silently when removing non-members" deleted with no replacement; nothing pins the integer-id semantics of `users.delete(Integer)`, hiding a potential 500 (P2, conf 75)
spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:100 — the controller spec dispatches the action directly, so the PUT-vs-DELETE verb mismatch passes even if the real route were removed (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In config/routes.rb the admin endpoint for removing a member is explicitly routed as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while the spec (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb around line ~100 in the diff) dispatches `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:90 — asserts only status 422, never that membership was unchanged; the require-before-guard ordering hazard is untested (P3, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec in the diff (context ".add_members" → "cannot add members to automatic groups") only asserts `response.status.should == 422` after calling `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"`. It indeed does not assert that group membership was unchanged, but that is a test-strength/narrow-coverage concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the code change. The finding’s “require-before-guard ordering hazard” is also framed as “untested” rather than pointing to a concrete failing behavior in the diff. Nothing in the diff demonstrates incorrect runtime behavior because of this missing assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20 — members was rewritten (limit 50, unconditional pagination, new envelope) with ZERO test changes; no groups_controller_spec exists at all (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does rewrite `GroupsController#members` to always paginate and to return an `{members, meta}` JSON envelope instead of a bare serialized array. However, the proposed finding’s core claim is about tests (“ZERO test changes; no groups_controller_spec exists at all”). From the diff alone we can only see that *admin* controller specs were changed; we cannot verify that no `groups_controller_spec` exists elsewhere in the repo, nor that tests weren’t updated in other files not shown. Also, lack of test changes is not itself a verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20 — the findMembers return-contract change plus new create/save/addMembers/removeMember and reshaped asJSON have no JS tests at all (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes substantial JS behavioral changes (e.g., Group#findMembers now mutates model state and may return `undefined` when name is empty; save/create endpoints and payload shape changed). However, the proposed finding claims this is a *problem* because there are “no JS tests at all.” The absence of JS tests is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff (no failing behavior is demonstrated, and no project requirement in the diff mandates JS tests). It’s a process/coverage suggestion rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness issue in the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8 — awaited afterModel replaced by a fire-and-forget setupController fetch; untested ordering/loading change (P3, conf 100)
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that an awaited/ordered fetch in afterModel was replaced with a fire-and-forget fetch in setupController, implying the member data may not be available when the controller runs (ordering/loading race). This matches the golden issue about the now-async, unhandled findMembers call causing a race condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — visible moved from nested to top-level param in one step: cached old admin JS PUTs flip every touched group to visible=false and drop its usernames while returning 200 (expand+contract violation) (P0, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes, the diff changes the Admin::GroupsController API from nested params (params[:group][:visible], params[:group][:name], params[:group][:usernames]) to top-level params (params[:visible], params[:name]) in both `create` and `update`.

In `update`, the new code unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. If an older admin JS client still sends `visible` under `group[...]` (or omits top-level `visible`), `params[:visible]` will be nil and this line will set `visible` to false, and the request can still return 200 via `success_json`.

Also, `update` no longer reads `params[:group][:usernames]` at all (membership changes moved to separate add/remove endpoints), so older JS PUTs that previously updated membership via `group[usernames]` will silently stop applying those changes while still returning success. The finding’s wording “drop its usernames” is slightly imprecise (it ignores the update rather than actively removing members), but the backward-compatibility/contract break and the `visible=false` flip are real and directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` may bypass GroupUser callbacks maintaining the denormalized groups.user_count, leaving permanent drift with no backfill and no test (P1, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff changes member removal from the previous pattern of calling a Group-level method (older code used `group.remove(user)` in membership changes) to `group.users.delete(user_id)`.

In Rails, `association.delete(...)` removes join rows without instantiating the join model and can bypass `destroy` callbacks / counter-cache style bookkeeping that custom `Group#remove` (or a `GroupUser` callback) would perform. This controller method also does not explicitly decrement/recompute `group.user_count` (a denormalized field heavily used in the new JS pagination), and the subsequent `group.save` won’t update `user_count` unless there is an unrelated callback elsewhere.

So the diff introduces a credible correctness risk: the persisted `groups.user_count` can drift after removals because the code path avoids the group’s membership-removal logic and uses a lower-level delete on the association.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — array-form usernames raise NoMethodError mid-loop with partially-applied adds not rolled back; typo'd names report full success (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` is followed by `usernames.split(",")`. If the client submits `usernames` as an array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `split` will raise `NoMethodError` (Array has no `split`) and the action will 500. Also, the loop silently ignores unknown usernames (`find_by_username` nil) and still renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, so typos/nonexistent usernames can be reported as full success. The “mid-loop”/rollback aspect isn’t directly verifiable here (the `split` error happens before the loop), but the type-crash and silent-success behavior are present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — unversioned response reshape on GET /groups/:group_id/members makes old cached clients render empty member lists during a rolling deploy (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the JSON shape returned by `GroupsController#members` from a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to an object with `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` (and also changes the client fetch URL to `/members.json`). This is a backwards-incompatible, unversioned response reshape on GET `/groups/:group_id/members`. An older cached client expecting an array (e.g., doing `result.map(...)`) would receive an object and fail to render the list (likely throwing or resulting in empty output) during a rolling deploy where old JS and new server coexist. This incompatibility is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — non-automatic groups previously returned all members; every existing API consumer now silently truncates at 50 (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the previous implementation only applied `limit/offset` for `group.automatic?` and otherwise returned the full ordered member list. The new code always applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset`, so non-automatic groups are now paginated and will return at most 50 members by default. Any client calling `/groups/:id/members` without providing `limit` will now receive a truncated list compared to before, which is a real behavioral/API compatibility change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — create never reads alias_level though the client sends it, so groups are created at alias_level 0 (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the client’s `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` includes `alias_level` and `create()` POSTs it to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `name` and `visible` and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]` (unlike `update`, which does). Therefore any alias level chosen client-side during creation will be ignored and the group will be created with the model default (commonly 0).
